notes: **Group 1:** Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr. One valence electron (ns$^1$). Extremely reactive, stored under oil to prevent reaction with air/moisture.

**Physical trends:** atomic radius increases down group; density increases except K is less dense than Na because atomic mass increases slower than atomic volume; melting and boiling points decrease down group; metallic character increases.
**Chemical trends:** reactivity increases down group because valence electron is farther from nucleus and easier to lose. All form +1 ions, white ionic compounds, strongly basic hydroxides.
**Flame colours:** Li crimson, Na golden yellow, K lilac, Rb red, Cs blue. Caused by electron excitation and emission at characteristic wavelengths.
**Diagonal relationship:** Li and Mg show similar properties (hardness, melting point, nitrides, carbonates) because of similar charge density ($Z/r$).
